title: Netanyahu Tells Mamdani 'Shame on You' as Dozens Walk Out of UN Speech; Abbas Calls Gaza War 'Genocidal' in Video Address
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday, September 24, 2026, as delegates from dozens of countries walked out before he began speaking. Netanyahu said Israel had carried out 'the opposite of genocide' in Gaza, told NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani directly 'Shame on you' for what he called distorting facts and inverting victim and aggressor, thanked President Trump as Israel's 'greatest partner,' downplayed West Bank settler violence as the work of roughly 150 'young offenders,' criticized Turkey as a 'super-spreader of antisemitic lies,' and gifted a Starlink device to Iran's UN delegation. Mamdani, citing Netanyahu's active International Criminal Court arrest warrant, said the speech was meant to 'sanitize his genocide of Palestinians.' The same day, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the Assembly by prerecorded video from his office in Ramallah after the US denied him and other Palestinian officials visas to attend in person for a second consecutive year, calling the war in Gaza a 'genocidal war' causing an 'unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe' and saying Israeli forces were responsible for 'killing, destruction, starvation and attempts at displacement.' Abbas said Trump's 20-point peace plan and the UN Security Council resolution endorsing it had 'not materialized on the ground.' Qatar's deputy chief of mission and Turkish officials separately rejected Netanyahu's criticism of mediating states.

confidenceReason: Netanyahu's and Abbas's UN General Assembly remarks, quotes and the mass walkout are corroborated by Al Jazeera, Haaretz, PBS NewsHour and The Times of Israel.

title: Israeli Fire Kills Five Palestinians in Gaza Over 24 Hours; Toll Reaches 73,928 Since October 2023
detail: Gaza's Health Ministry said Israeli fire killed five more Palestinians and wounded 35 others over the 24 hours to Thursday, September 24, 2026: Hasan Takreem al-Batta died in central Khan Younis of wounds sustained in an earlier attack; Rania Salama Saad was shot dead by Israeli soldiers in the al-Mawasi area of Rafah, southern Gaza; Muhannad Hosni Abu Medyin was shot dead west of az-Zahra in central Gaza; and Jabir Moqbel was killed in a strike near the American Hospital in az-Zawayda, his body reportedly struck a second time as relatives tried to transport it toward Gaza City, critically wounding two more relatives. A fifth victim was not immediately identified. The ministry put the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire at 1,408 killed and 4,916 wounded (834 bodies recovered), and the cumulative toll since October 7, 2023 at 73,928 killed and 175,030 wounded.
